name: International Protection (UNHCR Mandate Refugee Status Determination)

requirements.blocker_text: Must establish a well-founded fear of persecution in the country of origin to a UNHCR-conducted mandate refugee status determination interview.

sources.title: UNHCR Northern and Eastern Caribbean -- Apply for asylum through UNHCR: the British Virgin Islands is explicitly listed among the territories where UNHCR (via its regional office) conducts mandate refugee status determination at the request of the government, since no domestic asylum system exists locally; interview process, right to an interpreter and legal representation, appeal within 30 days of a negative decision

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of the British Virgin Islands' initial build. The BVI has NO domestic asylum/refugee-status-determination law or agency -- per this tier-2 UNHCR source, the Territory is explicitly grouped with Anguilla, Antigua and Barbuda, Barbados, and Bermuda as places where UNHCR itself conducts mandate refugee status determination at the government's request, rather than any BVI ministry or the Immigration Department (contrasted, per the same source, with the Bahamas, Cayman Islands, Jamaica, Montserrat, and Turks and Caicos Islands, where local governments handle asylum directly). Modelled as DRAFT for the same reasons as Antigua and Barbuda's equivalent route built earlier this session: tier-2 rather than tier-1 sourcing, and no confirmation of what local legal status (if any) follows a positive UNHCR determination -- work_rights, study_rights, and family_can_join are conservatively modelled as none/false pending that gap being closed.
